title: Spacing, Sizing, and Layout
description: Control element sizing and whitespace: master relative units (rem, %, vw/vh), min/max width constraints, margin collapse mechanics, and margin auto-centering.

objectives.statement: Constrain element dimensions using relative units (rem, %) and max-width boundaries for adaptive layouts.
Center block elements using margin: 0 auto and predict vertical margin collapse behavior between sibling blocks.

content.title: Fluid Sizing & Intelligent Spacing
content.hook: A fixed 800px width looks great on a desktop monitor, but on a smartphone screen it spills horizontally and breaks the layout. Modern layouts rely on fluid sizing and responsive constraints.
content.context: By combining `width: 100%` with `max-width: 720px` and `margin: 0 auto`, containers automatically stretch on mobile and gracefully lock at maximum readability on desktop. Meanwhile, understanding margin collapse explains why spacing between paragraphs doesn't double.
goals: Center block containers horizontally using `margin: 0 auto`.
Predict vertical margin collapse between sibling elements.

content.title: Vertical Margin Collapse in Action
content.description: Sibling Block A has `margin-bottom: 30px`. Sibling Block B has `margin-top: 20px`. The vertical distance between them collapses to the larger value (30px), NOT the sum (50px).

content.prompt: Two adjacent paragraph elements in normal flow have `margin-bottom: 32px` on the first paragraph and `margin-top: 16px` on the second paragraph. What is the actual vertical space between them on screen?
options: 32px (the margins collapse into a single margin equal to the largest margin)
16px (the smaller margin overrides the larger one)
0px (adjacent margins cancel out in standard flow)

validation.expected: 32px (the margins collapse into a single margin equal to the largest margin)

feedback.correct: Exactly right! In CSS normal block flow, adjacent vertical margins collapse into a single margin whose size is equal to the largest of the adjoining margins.
feedback.incorrect: Vertical margins between block elements collapse rather than accumulate. The resulting gap equals the larger margin (32px), not the sum.

content.title: Build a Centered Responsive Article Container
content.prompt:
Style the `.container` element:
1. Set `width: 100%` and constrain it with `max-width: 640px`.
2. Center it horizontally on screen using `margin: 0 auto`.
3. Add internal breathing room with `padding: 2rem`.
4. Give it a light background of `#f8fafc` and a border of `1px solid #e2e8f0`.
content.starterCode:
Fluid Container Layout

This container adapts fluidly to mobile screens and locks at 640px on large viewports.

feedback.correct: Outstanding! You built a battle-tested responsive container pattern: full width on mobile, locked max-width on desktop, and centered with auto margins.
feedback.incorrect: Check your properties: set `width: 100%`, `max-width: 640px`, `margin: 0 auto`, `padding: 2rem`, `background-color: #f8fafc`, and `border: 1px solid #e2e8f0`.

content.prompt: Why is using `rem` (root em) units for typography and spacing considered superior for user accessibility compared to hardcoded `px` values?

feedback.correct: Great analysis! `rem` units scale relative to the root `<html>` font-size setting. When visually impaired users adjust their browser's default font size, rem-based layouts scale proportionally without breaking.
feedback.incorrect: Think about users who change their browser's default font size preference for accessibility.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Spacing & Sizing
takeaways: Use rem units for accessible typography and consistent spacing scales.
Combine width: 100% with max-width to create fluid, readable content containers.
margin: 0 auto centers block elements horizontally inside their parent.
Adjacent vertical margins collapse into a single space equal to the larger margin.
